# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Terms defined in the book, with the chapter where each is introduced. Chapters are being added to
the glossary as they are revised to the house style, so the list is not yet complete.

| Term | Meaning | Introduced in |
|---|---|---|
| Antibiotic-associated diarrhoea (AAD) | Diarrhoea caused by antibiotic disruption of the gut microbiome | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Bacteriophage | A virus that infects bacteria; most viruses in the gut are bacteriophages | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Butyrogenic | Yielding a relatively high proportion of butyrate when fermented, as resistant starch does | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| *Clostridioides difficile* infection | Severe colitis caused by a toxin-producing bacterium that proliferates when the gut microbiome is depleted, usually by antibiotics | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Colonocyte | An epithelial cell lining the colon; its preferred fuel is butyrate | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Cross-feeding | One microbial species living on the products of another, as when butyrate producers use the lactate and acetate released by primary fibre degraders | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Dysbiosis | Disruption of the normal microbial community, for example by broad-spectrum antibiotics | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Enterotype | One of three discrete gut community types once proposed to classify everyone; now read as a continuous gradient | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Faecal microbiota transplant (FMT) | Transfer of stool from a healthy donor to restore a depleted gut community; proven only for recurrent *C. difficile* infection | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Fermentation | Anaerobic metabolism by bacteria in the colon of food the host's enzymes could not digest | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Fermented food | A food made through desired microbial growth and enzymatic conversions; it need not contain live microbes when eaten | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| FODMAPs | Fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides and polyols: short-chain carbohydrates that are rapidly fermented in the colon | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Functional redundancy | The capacity of many different microbial species to perform the same function, so that people with different species share a functional core | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Gut–brain axis | The two-way signalling between the gut and the brain, through the vagus nerve, short-chain fatty acids, the immune system and microbial metabolites | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Gut microbiome | The community of microbes (mostly bacteria, with some archaea, fungi and viruses) living in the gut, densest in the colon | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) | Sugars in breast milk that the infant cannot digest and that selectively feed *Bifidobacterium* | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Metagenome | The collective gene catalogue of the gut microbes, about 150 times the size of the human genome | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Methanogenic archaea | Archaea that consume hydrogen to produce methane, such as *Methanobrevibacter smithii* | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Microbial diversity | The number of different species present in a microbial community and how evenly they are represented | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Mucus barrier | The layer of mucus that keeps gut bacteria away from the epithelial surface | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Mycobiome | The fungal members of the gut microbial community | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Postbiotic | A preparation of inanimate microbes and/or their components that confers a health benefit | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Prebiotic | A substrate selectively used by host microorganisms conferring a health benefit; mostly fibres | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Probiotic | Live microorganisms that, when administered in adequate amounts, confer a health benefit | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Psychobiotic | A microbe or microbial product claimed to improve mental health | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) | Acetate, propionate and butyrate: the main products of colonic fermentation, which fuel the colonic epithelium and act as signals elsewhere in the body | *The Gut Microbiome* |
| Synbiotic | A combination of a probiotic and a prebiotic | *The Gut Microbiome* |
